findings.desc: The degraded single-host fallback eligibility is internally inconsistent enough to make later implementation ambiguous. docs/requirements/decisions/three-round-two-host-review-escalation-execution-plan.md:92 says degraded review is allowed only when a second host is demonstrably unavailable and policy allows it, and :112-115 requires attempted-host/provider plus observed unavailable condition. But :203-207, :766-775, and :829-834 describe explicit user-approved single-host local mode as an alternative to unavailable-host evidence, while :521-535 still requires unavailableSecondHostEvidencePresent. The artifact example at :333-350 also changes requiredAssurance to degraded-single-host, which blurs the original two-host requirement with the achieved lower assuranceLevel. Clarify whether user approval alone can substitute for unavailability evidence, and define required vs effective vs achieved assurance fields before implementation.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit f1581955f and revalidated in commit 661d7097e. The document now separates degraded fallback eligibility into unavailable-second-host and approved-single-host-local paths, clarifies which evidence belongs to each path, and splits requiredAssurance/effectiveAssurance/achievedAssurance so degraded review cannot be confused with the original two-host requirement.
